source.title: Extracting Unlearned Information from LLMs with Activation Steering
source.authors: Atakan Seyitoglu; A. Kuvshinov; Leo Schwinn; Stephan Günnemann

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some figure text is garbled in the extracted text, so figure-only numerical values cannot be reliably read.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether an activation-based intervention can recover information from unlearned models, using a different attack and retrieval measure from the unlearning methods themselves.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for activation steering on Harry Potter, TOFU, and ROME unlearning setups. It also describes prior work, but cited results are not included as rows. Parameter ablations used to choose the best setting are not recorded as outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study attacks existing unlearned models (WhoIsHarryPotter, TOFU, ROME) with an activation-steering intervention and measures recovery of the forgotten answers. That bears directly on C, a different method aimed at the same question. The unsteered WhoIsHarryPotter baseline also shows leakage under plain high-temperature sampling, which bears on A.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that AnonAct steering recovers unlearned broad knowledge (Harry Potter) but fails for narrow targets (TOFU authors, ROME single facts). They attribute the difference to the breadth and connectivity of the unlearned subject, and frame the result as a vulnerability of current unlearning.
record.recipe_differences: The paper tests an activation-steering extraction attack, not a recipe for unlearning. It evaluates WhoIsHarryPotter, TOFU unlearning, and ROME-edited facts.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies across unlearning setup and subject scope: Harry Potter recovery improves, while TOFU shows no improvement for almost all questions and ROME examples do not recover the original answers. The paper also explores coefficients, layers, and local versus global steering settings.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The main positive result uses a 62-question Harry Potter set and a keyword-frequency AUC rather than a direct accuracy measure. The TOFU result covers two fictitious authors, and the ROME recovery discussion gives two example prompts. The study does not report a general-ability check after unlearning.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Figure 3a and Figure 4 contain per-question CAF displays, but the extracted figure text is garbled, so individual values were not transcribed.

untested.parts: General-ability preservation after unlearning is not measured. Near-chance targeted accuracy is not established for TOFU or ROME.

The study uses addition of an anonymization-difference vector, not ablation of a direction. It offers no direct analysis showing blocked access versus deletion; the authors only hypothesize that unlearning severs links.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context attacks.
No new robust unlearning method is proposed or tested.

missing.what: Aggregate ROME result over the 20 CounterFact questions; only two example prompts are shown
Ablation results over coefficients, layers, and local vs global steering vectors. They are described but not reported, and bear on whether C depends on these choices

record.verdict_notes: This is a short workshop-style preprint. It reports no uncertainty and gives no TOFU or ROME AUC. The Harry Potter result rests on one 62-question set and one main configuration, chosen after parameter ablation. Version C names direction ablation, whereas this study adds a steering vector; I treat that as within C's 'internal edits' scope.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish near-chance targeted accuracy while preserving general ability, or test whether simple attacks fail.
No fine-tuning or relearning on small unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact datasets.
Uses activation addition/steering, not ablation of an activation direction. It does not directly establish that the unlearning method blocks access rather than deleting information.
No recovery by rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information alone.
Does not propose or test a newer unlearning method intended to resist the listed attacks.

relation.reason: Its own results on WHP, TOFU and ROME bear directly on whether internal edits recover unlearned knowledge (C).

tranche.reason: Anonymized activation-steering extraction is a different method aimed at the same question: is unlearned knowledge still recoverable?

source_check.notes: Steering is activation addition at the first token only, not ablation. The TOFU unlearning method is unnamed (TOFU codebase), and TOFU answers were converted to keywords. There is no code, control, capability check or uncertainty. The ROME evidence is two shown prompts, and Figures 3a/4 are garbled in the text.

statements.correction: 2411.02631, WHP model, 62 HP questions: no steering, T=2, top-k 40, 2000 samples per question, keyword-frequency ROC AUC 0.75 (authors: better than random; leakage without intervention); base Llama2-7B-chat 0.98. No greedy-decoding comparison.
statements.problem: Cites r1, but none of its WHP numbers or settings (greedy vs top-p, 1024 samples, 38%, 100 samples, 27.8% vs 3.6%) appear in this text. It never gives this study's own result. The theme (sampling reveals leakage) fits r1.

statements.correction: 2411.02631 also ran additive AnonAct steering on a TOFU-unlearned Phi-1.5 model (40 questions). CAF was lower or the same for almost all questions. No direction ablation was run.
statements.problem: Minor omission only: the basis lists 2606.03291 as the only steering test on TOFU. This study also steered on TOFU. What it says about this study (additive steering on WHP, no ablation) is right.
